prompt: I have 3 days in Hong Kong in November. Where should I stay and what should I do without renting a car?
expected: Load visitor-lodging, visitor-itineraries, transport; recommend Island/Kowloon base by style; MTR+Octopus first; point to attractions/itineraries; avoid inventing live fares.
actual: For a three-day November visit, pick one harbour-side base and ride MTR + Octopus instead of renting a car. Stay in Tsim Sha Tsui or Causeway Bay if you want walkable food and easy cross-harbour hops; choose Central/Sheung Wan if you want Island nightlife and Mid-Levels access. Day 1: harbour views + one Peak or trail block and a neighborhood dinner. Day 2: Kowloon markets/museums plus a night view. Day 3: outlying island or a Macau day trip only after checking separate entry rules. I would load references/visitor-lodging.md, references/visitor-itineraries.md, and references/transport.md, and re-check MTR/Octopus pages before quoting fares.

prompt: I am 27 from Australia and want a Working Holiday in Hong Kong. Can I work for the same cafe for the whole year?
expected: Load visas.md and sources.md; explain ImmD Note 2 is nationality-specific; Australia same-employer cap is three months on the checked ImmD page; do not use a generic >6 months rule; require live ImmD re-check.
actual: Working Holiday rules are orientation-only until re-checked on ImmD. For Australian citizens, the ImmD Working Holiday Scheme Note 2 snapshot says you are not allowed to work for the same employer for more than three months—not a full year at one cafe, and not a generic six-month same-employer rule. Study/training caps and funds proof also vary by nationality (Notes 3–4). I would open references/visas.md and references/sources.md and re-check https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/visas/working_holiday_scheme.html for your passport before you apply or accept a long single-employer plan.
bm25_prompt: Hong Kong Working Holiday Australia same employer limit ImmD

prompt: I got a tech job offer in Hong Kong. Is Causeway Bay or Discovery Bay better if I want nightlife sometimes but also a quieter home?

actual: Causeway Bay/Wan Chai puts nightlife and MTR convenience next door, so evenings out are easy but home is less quiet.
